# Postfold

> Postfold is an iPhone and iPad app that saves posts from X into folders you create, with your own titles and notes. It has no login of any kind and no third-party analytics, shows ads from Google AdMob, and syncs through the user's private iCloud. Requires iOS 18 or later.

This is the Postfold product site at [postfold.space](https://postfold.space). Markdown versions of each page are linked below for AI assistants and LLMs.

Key facts:
- Saves posts from X into user-created folders (bookmark folders are a Premium-only feature on X)
- Save in two taps from the iOS Share sheet, or by copying a post link
- Custom titles, private notes, emoji and color for folders
- Sort by date added, date modified, title, date posted or author; filter by date range, author, note or status
- List, compact and grid layouts; search across post text, authors, titles and notes
- No login: never connects to an X account, no Postfold account, no X API, no scraping
- Post content comes only from X's public oEmbed service; the details screen shows X's official embed with "do not track" on
- Library stored on device (SwiftData) and synced through the user's private iCloud (CloudKit); the developer runs no server and never receives the user's posts, notes or folders
- Ads come from Google AdMob (banner on post details, ads between posts in the list, occasional full-screen ad after adding a post), behind Google's consent form and the iOS tracking prompt; ad requests never include the user's posts, notes or folders
- Crash reports and usage statistics come only through Apple's built-in tools (MetricKit, Xcode Organizer, App Store Connect), without the user's identity, with an opt-out in the app's Settings
- Deleted posts are marked Unavailable; the user's link, title, note and folder are kept
- An Android version keeps the library on the device (Android backup, no sync) and uses Google Firebase for crash reports and usage statistics; see the Privacy Policy
- Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by X Corp.
- Status: coming soon to the App Store

# Your saved posts, finally in folders.

Postfold saves posts from X into folders you create, with your own titles and notes. No login, no account, no server. Your library syncs through your private iCloud.

Coming soon to the App Store

- No login
- No account
- iCloud sync
- iPhone & iPad
- iOS 18+

Bookmark folders on X are a Premium feature. **Postfold gives every saved post a home**, without signing in to anything.

Features

## Everything you save, organized your way

Folders, titles, notes, sorting and search for the posts you want to come back to.

### Save in two taps

Share a post from the X app, pick a folder, done. Add a note right in the Share sheet.

### A folder for every idea

Create as many folders as you like, each with its own emoji and color, plus a live post count.

### Make every save yours

Give posts your own title and a private note, so you remember why you saved them.

### Sort and filter your way

Sort by date added, date modified, title, date posted or author. Filter by date range, author, note or status.

### List, compact or grid

Pick the layout that fits the folder. On iPad, folders, posts and details sit side by side.

### Find anything fast

Search across post text, authors, your titles and your notes.

### Synced with iCloud

Your library follows you across iPhone and iPad through your private iCloud. No sign-up.

### Handles deleted posts

If a post disappears from X, Postfold marks it Unavailable and keeps your link, title and note.

### Copied a link? Save it

Open Postfold after copying a post link and a banner offers to save it. The clipboard is only read when you tap Paste.

How it works

## Share, pick a folder, done

### Tap Share on a post

In the X app, tap Share on any post and choose Postfold. Or just copy the post's link.

### Pick a folder

Choose a folder (or create one), add a note if you like, and tap Save.

### Find it later

Open Postfold to sort, filter and search your saves. Tap Open in X to read the post in the X app.

[Where your data goes](https://postfold.space/how-it-works/)

Screenshots

## Made for iPhone and iPad

Swipe to see more. Tap a screenshot to enlarge it.

Private by design

## No login. No account. No server.

Postfold is built so there is nothing to sign in to, and your content never leaves your devices and your iCloud.

### Nothing to sign in to

Postfold never asks for your X password and never connects to your X account. There is no Postfold account either.

### Your iCloud, not our server

Folders, posts and notes stay on your devices and in your private iCloud. The developer cannot see them.

### Ads never see your library

Postfold shows ads from Google AdMob. Advertisers never receive your posts, notes or folders, and you choose whether ads can be personalized. Crash reports come only through Apple's built-in tools, and you can turn them off.

[Read the Privacy Policy](https://postfold.space/privacy/)

FAQ

## Questions, answered

### Do I need to sign in to X or create an account?

No. Postfold has no login of any kind: it never connects to your X account and there is no Postfold account. You save a post by sharing it from the X app or by pasting its link.

### Can Postfold import the bookmarks I already have on X?

No. Because Postfold never signs in to X, it cannot read your X bookmarks. You add posts one at a time, from the Share sheet or by pasting a link.

### How do I save a post?

In the X app, tap Share on a post, then choose Postfold. Pick a folder, add a note if you like, and tap Save. You can also copy a post link and open Postfold: a banner offers to save it, or you can paste it on the Add screen.

### Are my folders synced between my iPhone and iPad?

Yes. Postfold syncs through your own private iCloud, so every device signed in to the same Apple Account sees the same folders, posts and notes. If iCloud is turned off, everything stays on that device.

### What happens when a post is deleted on X?

Postfold re-checks saved posts from time to time. If a post is no longer available, it is marked Unavailable and its cached text is removed. Your link, custom title, note and folder are kept.

### Does Postfold collect any data?

Not your content. Your posts, notes and folders stay on your devices and in your private iCloud, and they are never shared with advertisers. Postfold shows ads from Google AdMob, which uses device data such as your IP address, how you interact with ads and, if you allow tracking, your device's advertising identifier. To fix bugs, we receive anonymous crash reports and usage statistics through Apple's built-in tools. You can turn them off in Postfold's Settings and in iOS Settings. The Privacy Policy has the details.

### Does it work on iPad?

Yes. Postfold runs on iPhone and iPad with iOS 18 or later. On iPad you see folders, posts and the post itself side by side.

### How much does Postfold cost?

Any price or in-app purchase is shown on the App Store listing before you download or buy.

### Is Postfold made by X?

No. Postfold is an independent app and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by X Corp.

## Give your saved posts a home

Postfold for iPhone and iPad. Requires iOS 18 or later.

Coming soon to the App Store

<!-- https://postfold.space/how-it-works/ -->

# How Postfold works

Postfold keeps your saved posts organized without an account, a login or a server. Here's what happens when you save, view and open a post, and where each piece of data goes.

**Your iPhone or iPad** Stores your folders, titles, notes and a cached copy of each post.

**Your private iCloud** Syncs your library between your devices. Only you can read it.

**X's public embed service** Receives a post's link and returns its text and embed. Nothing else.

There is no Postfold server. The developer never receives your posts, notes or folders.

## 1. Saving a post

Tap Share on a post in the X app and choose Postfold, or copy the post's link and open Postfold. The Share sheet only shows your folders and a note field; the link, folder and note are passed to the main app on your device.

When the app opens, it adds the post and asks X's public oEmbed service (`publish.x.com/oembed`) for it, sending just the post's link with "do not track" on. It caches the author, text and embed so your library loads instantly and works offline.

## 2. Organizing

Folders, custom titles, notes, sorting and filtering all happen on your device. Each folder remembers its own sort order and filters. The date a post was published is worked out from the post's ID, so no extra request is needed.

## 3. Viewing a post

The details screen shows X's official embedded post, exactly as X publishes it, with "do not track" on. Links inside the embed open in the X app or Safari, never in a browser inside Postfold.

## 4. Keeping posts up to date

From time to time, including in the background, Postfold re-checks a small batch of older saves with the same embed service. If a post was deleted or made private, it becomes Unavailable: the cached text is removed, and your link, title, note and folder stay.

## 5. Syncing

With iCloud on, your library syncs through the private CloudKit database in your own iCloud account. If two devices save the same post while offline, Postfold merges the duplicates when it next opens.

## 6. Crash reports

To find bugs, Postfold relies on tools built into iOS. If you allow it in iOS Settings, Apple shares anonymous crash reports and usage statistics with the developer, and iOS gives the app performance summaries on your device. None of this includes your posts, links, titles or notes, and you can turn it off in Postfold's Settings. The [Privacy Policy](https://postfold.space/privacy/) has the details.

## 7. Ads

Postfold shows ads from Google AdMob: a banner under a post's details, ads between posts in the list, and sometimes a full-screen ad after you add a post. Where the law requires it, the app asks for your consent first, and iOS asks whether Postfold may track you. If you say no, ads still appear, but without your device's advertising identifier. Ad requests never include your posts, links, titles, notes or folders. The [Privacy Policy](https://postfold.space/privacy/) has the details.

## What Postfold never does

| Postfold never… | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| asks you to log in to X or to Postfold | No password to leak, no account to manage. |
| uses the X API or scrapes x.com | Only X's public, documented embed service is used. |
| downloads images or videos | Media is shown by X's official embed, from X. |
| opens posts in an in-app browser | Posts open in the X app or Safari, where you're already signed in. |
| shares your library with advertisers | Ads come from Google AdMob, and ad requests never include your posts, links, titles, notes or folders. |
| includes third-party analytics or crash reporting | Crash and usage reports come only through Apple's built-in tools, without your identity, and you can turn them off. |

Want the technical details? Read about [the technology behind Postfold](https://postfold.space/technology/), or the full [Privacy Policy](https://postfold.space/privacy/).

<!-- https://postfold.space/technology/ -->

# Technology

Postfold is a native Apple app. Here is what it's built with and why.

### SwiftUI & Swift 6

A fully native interface for iPhone and iPad, written in Swift 6 with strict concurrency checking.

### SwiftData + CloudKit

Your library is stored with SwiftData and synced through the private CloudKit database in your iCloud.

### Apple frameworks first

Apple frameworks everywhere except ads, which use the Google Mobile Ads SDK and its consent library. No analytics or crash-reporting libraries from other companies.

## Architecture

- **App + Share Extension.** The Share Extension never opens the database. It reads a small list of your folders and drops each new save into an inbox in a shared App Group container. The main app imports the inbox when it opens. This keeps the extension fast and avoids two processes writing to the same store.
- **Shared Swift package.** Link parsing, oEmbed parsing, models and the sort/filter query live in one local package used by both the app and the extension.
- **CloudKit-friendly model.** Every field has a default and relationships are optional, as CloudKit requires. Duplicates created by offline saves on two devices are merged on launch.

## Content from X, done by the book

- **oEmbed only.** Post text and embed markup come from X's public oEmbed endpoint, requested with `dnt=true` and `omit_script=true`. Responses are parsed without loading HTML into a web view.
- **Official embed.** The details screen renders the oEmbed HTML with X's `widgets.js` in a `WKWebView`. Every link tap is handed to iOS, which opens the X app or Safari.
- **Post dates from IDs.** X post IDs encode their creation time, so Postfold can sort by date posted without any extra request.
- **Polite re-checks.** A background refresh task re-checks a small batch of the oldest saves, one request at a time.

## Privacy, verified

- Ads come from the Google Mobile Ads SDK, behind Google's consent form and the iOS tracking prompt. The app's privacy manifest declares tracking for that reason, and ad requests carry nothing from your library.
- Crash and performance diagnostics use Apple's MetricKit and Xcode Organizer, with an opt-out in Settings. No third-party service receives them.
- Clipboard detection asks iOS for a yes/no "is there probably a link?" answer, so no paste prompt appears and nothing is read until you tap Paste.
- Apart from Google's ad services, the only network hosts the app talks to are X's embed services.

## Requirements

iPhone or iPad with iOS 18 or later. Some interface touches use iOS 26 features when available.

# How can we help?

Answers to common questions, plus a direct line to the developer.

### Contact support

Questions, feedback or feature ideas. Write to huynguyennovem@gmail.com.

[Email us](mailto:huynguyennovem@gmail.com?subject=Postfold%20support)

### Report a bug

Tell us what happened and the steps to reproduce it. Include your device, iOS version and the app version from Settings › About.

[Send a bug report](mailto:huynguyennovem@gmail.com?subject=Postfold%20bug%20report&body=Device%3A%20%0AiOS%20version%3A%20%0APostfold%20version%3A%20%0A%0AWhat%20happened%3A%20%0A%0ASteps%20to%20reproduce%3A%20)

### Privacy questions

Postfold never receives your posts, notes or folders. Read how it works, or email us about anything privacy-related.

[Privacy Policy](https://postfold.space/privacy/)

## Getting started

1. Open Postfold once and create a few folders (or keep everything in Unsorted).
2. In the X app, tap Share on a post, then Share via…, and choose Postfold.
3. Pick a folder, add a note if you like, and tap Save.
4. Open Postfold to see your saved post, sort, filter and search.

Prefer copying links? Copy a post link anywhere, open Postfold, and tap Paste on the banner. You can also tap + and paste a link on the Add screen.

## Troubleshooting

### Postfold doesn't appear in the Share sheet

Open Postfold once after installing it. Then, in the X app, tap Share, then Share via…, scroll the row of apps to the end, tap More, and turn on Postfold. You can drag it to the top of the list.

### The Share sheet says my folders will appear later

The Share sheet reads your folder list from the main app. Open Postfold once and your folders will show up the next time you share.

### I saved a post but it isn't in the app yet

Posts saved from the Share sheet are added the next time you open Postfold. If it still doesn't appear, check that you have an internet connection so the app can load the post.

### Postfold says the link isn't a post

Postfold saves links to single posts, such as x.com/name/status/1234567890. Links to profiles, lists or searches can't be saved.

### A post shows as Unavailable

The post was deleted, or its account is now private or suspended, so X no longer returns it. Your link, title, note and folder are kept. If you think it's a mistake, open the post and tap Reload Post.

### My library isn't syncing between devices

Make sure every device is signed in to the same Apple Account and that iCloud is turned on for Postfold. In Postfold, open Settings and check that Storage says iCloud. Sync can take a few minutes, and needs an internet connection.

### The post details screen is blank

The embedded post loads from X, so it needs an internet connection. Tap Reload Post to try again. You can always tap Open in X to read the post in the X app or Safari.

## Still stuck?

Email [huynguyennovem@gmail.com](mailto:huynguyennovem@gmail.com). We usually reply within a few days. Postfold is made by one independent developer, so thank you for your patience.

Looking for general questions? See the [FAQ on the home page](https://postfold.space/#faq).

# Privacy Policy

Last updated: November 10, 2026

This page explains what Postfold stores, where it is stored, which outside services it talks to, and what crash, usage and advertising information is collected. The iPhone and iPad app and the Android app differ, so each section says which app it describes. Section 8 covers advertising, and section 9 covers what only the Android app does.

**In short:** Postfold has no account and no login. We never see the posts, links, titles, notes or folders you save: they stay on your devices and, on iPhone and iPad, in your private iCloud. To show a post, the app asks X's public embed service for it. The app shows ads through Google AdMob, which can use your device's advertising identifier; on iPhone and iPad, only if you allow tracking. Advertisers never receive anything from your library. On iPhone and iPad, there is no third-party analytics: anonymous crash reports and usage statistics reach us through Apple's built-in tools, and you can turn them off. On Android, crash reports and usage statistics go to Google Firebase, and you can turn them off too.

## 1. Who we are

Postfold is an app for iPhone, iPad and Android developed by Huy Nguyen ("we", "us"). If you have any question about this policy, email [huynguyennovem@gmail.com](mailto:huynguyennovem@gmail.com).

## 2. Information we collect

On every platform, we never receive the content of your library, we do not operate servers for the app, and the app has no user accounts and no sign-in, with X or with us.

**On iPhone and iPad** the app includes one outside service, Google AdMob, which shows ads and collects advertising data, described in section 8. The app has no third-party analytics or crash-reporting SDKs. Apart from advertising, the only information about how the app runs that reaches us is anonymous crash reports, diagnostics and usage statistics provided by Apple, described in section 5.

**On Android** the app includes two Google services, AdMob and Firebase. They collect device identifiers (including the advertising ID), advertising data, crash reports and usage statistics, described in sections 8 and 9.

## 3. What the app stores, and where

To work, Postfold keeps your library on your device:

- the links of the posts you save, and the author name and handle;
- a cached copy of each post's text and embed markup, as returned by X's embed service;
- your folders, custom titles and notes, and the dates you added or changed them;
- your app settings (for example the default layout and folder).

**iCloud sync (iPhone and iPad).** If iCloud is turned on for your Apple Account, this library is synced through the private CloudKit database in *your* iCloud account, so it appears on your other devices. It is stored and protected by Apple under [Apple's Privacy Policy](https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/). We have no access to your iCloud data. If iCloud is off, the library stays on that device only.

**Share extension (iPhone and iPad).** When you save from the Share sheet, the link, folder and note are handed to the main app through a shared container on your device. Nothing leaves the device at this step.

**Android.** The library stays on your device and does not sync between devices. Section 9 explains Android backup.

## 4. Connections to X

Postfold never signs in to X, does not use the X API and does not scrape x.com. It contacts X only in these cases:

- **Saving and re-checking a post.** The app sends the post's link to X's public oEmbed service at `publish.x.com/oembed`, with the "do not track" option turned on, and caches the result. It does this when you save a post and, from time to time, to check that saved posts still exist (including in the background, when the system allows it).
- **Viewing a post.** The post details screen shows X's official embedded post. It loads X's embed script from `platform.twitter.com`, again with "do not track" on, and the post's images, videos and profile pictures come from X's servers.
- **Opening a post.** Tapping Open in X hands the link to iOS or Android, which opens it in the X app or in your browser. Postfold has no in-app browser.

Like any web request, these connections let X see your IP address and basic device information. X handles that data under its own [Privacy Policy](https://x.com/en/privacy), not this one.

## 5. Crash reports and usage statistics on iPhone and iPad

To see when Postfold crashes or runs slowly, and how many people use it, the iPhone and iPad app relies on tools built into iOS and provided by Apple. It does not add any third-party service for this.

- **Crash reports and diagnostics.** If you turned on *Share With App Developers* in iOS (Settings › Privacy & Security › Analytics & Improvements), Apple sends us crash logs and reports about hangs, performance, energy and disk use for Postfold, through Xcode and App Store Connect.
- **Usage statistics.** App Store Connect shows us aggregated figures such as installs, sessions, active devices, retention and crash counts, for people who agreed to share analytics with app developers. We see totals, not individuals.
- **On-device diagnostics.** Through Apple's MetricKit framework, iOS also gives Postfold daily summaries of how the app performed on your device, such as launch time, memory use, hangs and crash call stacks. Postfold uses them to spot problems. They stay on your device and Postfold does not upload them.

These reports contain technical information only, such as the device model, iOS version, app version and the call stack of the app's own code. They never include the posts, links, titles, notes or folders you save, and Apple does not tell us who you are. Apple handles this data under its [Privacy Policy](https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/).

**How to turn it off.** Turn off the crash and diagnostics option in Postfold's Settings to stop Postfold from collecting on-device diagnostics. To stop sharing crash and usage data with all app developers, turn off *Share With App Developers* in iOS Settings › Privacy & Security › Analytics & Improvements.

## 6. Clipboard

When you open the app with "Detect Copied Links" turned on, Postfold asks iOS or Android whether the clipboard probably contains a web link. The system answers without revealing the content. The clipboard is only read when you tap Paste. You can turn this off in Postfold's Settings.

## 7. Deleted posts

If X reports that a post no longer exists or is no longer public, Postfold marks it Unavailable and deletes the cached text and embed. Your link, title, note and folder are kept until you delete them.

## 8. Advertising

Postfold shows ads provided by Google AdMob on iPhone, iPad and Android: a banner on the post details screen, ads between posts in the list, and sometimes a full-screen ad after you add a post. The Share sheet shows no ads.

To deliver and measure ads and to limit fraud, Google collects your IP address (which shows your approximate location), device information such as the model and system version, how you interact with ads and, when it is available, your device's advertising identifier. Google's ads software also sends Google diagnostic data about itself, such as crash and performance data. Google and its advertising partners may use this information to show personalized ads. See [How Google uses information from sites or apps that use its services](https://policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites) and [Google's Privacy Policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy).

Postfold never sends advertisers anything from your library: ad requests carry no post links, authors, titles, notes or folder names.

**Consent.** Where the law requires it, for example in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland, Postfold shows Google's consent form and requests no ad until you have made your choices. Where the form applies to you, you can reopen it at any time under Privacy Options in Postfold's Settings.

**Tracking on iPhone and iPad.** iOS asks whether you allow Postfold to track you. If you allow it, Google can use your device's advertising identifier to personalize ads and to measure them across apps and websites owned by other companies. If you decline, ads still appear, but Postfold cannot read the identifier. You can change your answer in iOS Settings › Privacy & Security › Tracking.

**Advertising ID on Android.** The Android app lets Google read the device's advertising ID. You can reset or delete it in Android Settings (Privacy › Ads, or Google › Ads on some devices). Once it is deleted, apps, including Postfold, no longer receive it.

## 9. Postfold for Android

Sections 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8 also describe the Android app. This section covers what is different on Android.

**Storage and backup.** The Android app keeps your library on your device only. There is no sync between devices. If backup is turned on for your Google Account, Android includes Postfold's library and settings in your device backup, so they can be restored when you reinstall the app or move to a new phone. That backup is stored and protected by Google under [Google's Privacy Policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy). We have no access to it.

**Saving from the Share sheet.** The link, folder and note are saved directly into the library on your device.

**Crash reports and usage statistics (Google Firebase).** The Android app uses Firebase Crashlytics and Google Analytics for Firebase, both provided by Google.

- **Crash reports** contain the call stack of the app's code, the device model, Android version and app version, and an installation identifier created by Firebase.
- **Usage statistics** count a few actions, such as saving a post, creating or deleting a folder, or a saved post becoming unavailable. These events carry no details. Google Analytics also collects, automatically, app opens and sessions, the device model, Android version, app version and language, your approximate region derived from your IP address, an app-instance identifier and your device's advertising ID.

These reports never include the posts, links, author names, titles, notes or folder names you save. Google processes this data under the [Firebase privacy terms](https://firebase.google.com/support/privacy) and [Google's Privacy Policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy).

**How to turn it off.** Turn off Collect Diagnostics in Postfold's Settings. Postfold then stops sending crash reports and usage statistics, and deletes crash reports that were not sent yet.

## 10. This website

This website is a static site hosted on GitHub Pages. GitHub may log visitors' IP addresses for security, as described in the [GitHub Privacy Statement](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement).

We use [Cloudflare Web Analytics](https://www.cloudflare.com/web-analytics/) to count page views on this website. It does not use cookies or local storage, does not track you across sites, and reports only aggregate statistics such as page views, referrers and country. It is not used in the app. Fonts and images are served from this site; we set no cookies.

## 11. Your choices and rights

On iPhone and iPad:

- Delete a post or folder in the app to remove it from your devices and iCloud.
- Delete the app to remove its local data. To remove the synced copy, manage Postfold's data in your iCloud storage settings on iPhone, iPad or Mac.
- Turn off iCloud for Postfold to keep the library on one device.
- Turn off Background App Refresh for Postfold in iOS Settings to stop background re-checks.
- Turn off the crash and diagnostics option in Postfold's Settings, or *Share With App Developers* in iOS, to stop crash and usage reports (see section 5).
- Turn off tracking for Postfold in iOS Settings › Privacy & Security › Tracking, or change your ad choices under Privacy Options in Postfold's Settings where it is shown (see section 8).

On Android:

- Delete a post or folder in the app to remove it from your device.
- Delete the app to remove its local data. To remove the backup copy, manage backups in your Google Account.
- Turn off Collect Diagnostics in Postfold's Settings to stop crash reports and usage statistics (see section 9).
- Change your ad choices under Privacy Options in Postfold's Settings where it is shown, or reset or delete your advertising ID in Android Settings (see section 8).
- Restrict background use for Postfold in Android Settings to limit background re-checks.

We run no servers and hold no copy of your library. On iPhone and iPad, crash and usage reports reach us without your identity. Advertising data on every platform, and Firebase data on Android, is held by Google and tied to identifiers such as an advertising identifier or an installation identifier, not to your name; we see it as crash reports and aggregate statistics.

Postfold does not sell the content of your library or pass it to anyone. Showing personalized ads through Google may count as "selling" or "sharing" personal information under some privacy laws; you can opt out with the controls above. If you have a privacy request or concern, email [huynguyennovem@gmail.com](mailto:huynguyennovem@gmail.com) and we will reply.

## 12. Children

Postfold is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children.

## 13. Security

All network connections use HTTPS. Data synced through iCloud is protected by Apple's iCloud security.

## 14. Changes to this policy

If the app's data practices change, for example if a new feature needs a new service, we will update this page and the date at the top before the change ships.

## 15. Contact

Huy Nguyen Email: [huynguyennovem@gmail.com](mailto:huynguyennovem@gmail.com)

# Terms of Use

Last updated: November 7, 2026

These terms apply to the Postfold app and this website. Please read them before using Postfold.

## 1. Agreement

By downloading or using Postfold, you agree to these Terms of Use and to our [Privacy Policy](https://postfold.space/privacy/). Postfold is licensed, not sold, to you through the Apple App Store. Your use is also governed by Apple's [Licensed Application End User License Agreement](https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/) (the "Standard EULA"). If these terms and the Standard EULA conflict, the Standard EULA applies.

## 2. What Postfold does

Postfold lets you save links to public posts from X, organize them in folders, and add your own titles and notes. Post content is shown through X's public oEmbed service and official embed. Postfold does not sign in to X, does not use the X API and does not download images or videos.

## 3. Not affiliated with X

Postfold is an independent app. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by X Corp. "X" is a trademark of X Corp. and is used only to describe the content Postfold works with.

## 4. Content from X

Posts belong to their authors and are provided by X. We do not control, review or endorse them. Your use of X's content and services, including the X app and website, is subject to [X's Terms of Service](https://x.com/en/tos). Postfold relies on X's public services; if X changes or stops them, some features may stop working, and posts deleted or made private on X become Unavailable in the app.

## 5. Your content and your data

Your folders, titles and notes are yours. They are stored on your devices and, if you use iCloud, in your iCloud account. We do not have a copy and cannot recover lost data, so keep iCloud or device backups if your library matters to you. You are responsible for the notes you write and the posts you choose to save.
